title: Buy, set up and design like a professional maker

say: Buy, set up and design like a professional maker.
This is the video for Module 1 of Advanced Beadwork and Jewellery Making: professional materials, tools and design.
In the beginner course you strung beads onto cord and wire. Advanced work is different.
In bead weaving, every bead touches its neighbours, so uneven beads show immediately.

say: In wire work, the metal touches skin all day. The wrong metal causes green marks, tarnish or itchy ears. So buying well is the first professional skill.

say: Findings are the metal parts: clasps, jump rings, ear wires and head pins. Read the stamp.
Sterling silver is 92.5% silver, mixed with another metal, usually copper, for strength.

panel.heading: Findings and metals
items: Sterling silver: 92.5% silver
14/20 GF: 14 karat gold is 5% of the weight
Gold-plated wears off: describe it honestly
Copper and brass: good for practice, can mark skin
Ear wires: nickel-free, sterling, titanium or niobium

say: 14/20 G F means gold-filled: 14 karat gold bonded to brass, making up one twentieth, or 5%, of the weight. It lasts for years.

say: Nickel is one of the most common causes of skin allergy from jewellery. For earrings, use ear wires sold as nickel-free, or sterling silver, titanium or niobium, and tell the customer which metal you used.

say: Beads per gram change with brand and finish, so count a sample yourself on a digital scale that reads to 0.01 g.
Step one. Find how many beads your pattern needs.

Weigh 1 g and count it in groups of ten
Divide to find the grams you need
Add 10% spare
Round up to whole packs

panel.rule: Buy the whole amount from one batch, at the same time.

say: Here is a worked example. Halima in Kaduna plans a peyote cuff. Her pattern needs about 3,000 cylinder beads in her main colour.

panel.heading: Cylinder beads for a peyote cuff
items: Count 1 g of beads: 186
Buy 4 tubes of 5 g (20 g), one batch

say: She weighs out 1 g of her beads and counts them: 186 beads.

panel.heading: Cylinder beads for a peyote cuff
items: Count 1 g of beads: 186
Buy 4 tubes of 5 g (20 g), one batch

say: 3,000 divided by 186 gives 16.1 g.

panel.heading: Cylinder beads for a peyote cuff
items: Count 1 g of beads: 186
Buy 4 tubes of 5 g (20 g), one batch

say: She adds about 10%: 16.1 times 1.1 gives 17.7 g.

panel.heading: Cylinder beads for a peyote cuff
items: Count 1 g of beads: 186
Buy 4 tubes of 5 g (20 g), one batch

say: The seller packs this colour in 5 g tubes. 17.7 divided by 5 is 3.5, so she buys 4 tubes, which is 20 g, all from one batch. She will not run short halfway through.

say: Put the flat side of your flush cutters toward the wire you keep, then feel the end and file it if it catches.
Cut ends can fly, so wear safety glasses, point the cutter down and cover the short end.

panel.heading: Cutting wire safely
left: Point cutter down, cover the end
right: Cut memory wire with jewellery cutters
Use pliers with teeth on wire

say: Never cut steel memory wire with jewellery cutters; it dents the blades. Keep offcuts in a jar, away from children and bare feet. And use smooth-jawed pliers, because teeth mark wire.

panel.heading: Cutting wire safely
left: Point cutter down, cover the end
right: Cut memory wire with jewellery cutters
Use pliers with teeth on wire

say: Give each piece one focal point and keep the rest quieter. Photograph it in black and white. If your eye goes to one spot first, it works.

panel.heading: What makes a piece look intentional
items: One focal point, everything else quieter
Princess length, 43 to 48 cm, is the safe default
Bracelets: snug wrist plus about 1.5 to 2 cm
Weigh earrings and wear them for two hours
Use African traditions with respect and honesty

say: Princess length, 43 to 48 cm, sits just below the collarbone and suits most necklines.

say: For beaded bracelets, measure the wrist snugly and add about 1.5 to 2 cm. Record the customer's measurement, not just the size you made.

say: Weigh each earring and wear the pair for two hours. If your lobe feels pulled, that is the common mistake: make it lighter or use a supported post.

say: Use African bead traditions as inspiration with respect. Say honestly what your piece is, for example, inspired by Ndebele colour blocking, rather than claiming it is traditional.

say: To remember. Bead sizes run backwards, so 15/0 is tiny. Read the metal stamp and describe plated pieces honestly. Use nickel-free ear wires. Count a 1 g sample, add 10% and buy from one batch. And protect your eyes when you cut wire.

panel.heading: Remember
items: 15/0 is smaller than 11/0, which is smaller than 8/0
Read the stamp: sterling, 14/20 GF or plated
Nickel-free ear wires; tell customers the metal
Count 1 g, add 10%, buy from one batch
Glasses on and flat side in when cutting wire
